code_revision_note: git HEAD at generation time (manifest generated before commit; not the eventual commit SHA)
invariant_parameters: source facts (pinned revision, raw bytes, raw SHA-256, canonical content)
forecast models and model versions (naive, moving_average, ses, hist_gradient_boosting)
candidate policy families and policy versions
temporal folds (expanding origins; final test untouched)
observed selection-window semantics (last validation fold demand, observed sales; censored demand during stockouts is documented, not recovered)

baseline-v1.description: Reproduces the current v2 decisions exactly: service target 0.90, lead 3, review 1, cost multipliers 1.0, demand scale 1.0.
baseline-v1.label: Exact current reference
baseline-v1.rationale: The baseline must reproduce the current v2 decisions byte-for-byte and serves as the comparison reference for every other scenario.

costs-low.description: Holding, stockout, and ordering multipliers all 0.5; everything else identical to baseline.
costs-low.label: All costs halved
costs-low.rationale: A uniform cost deflation keeps relative cost ordering but changes absolute magnitudes; checks that selection is not scale-driven.

demand-stress-high.description: Controlled demand scale 1.30 applied to the deployment/simulation stress window ONLY; source demand, forecast training, and the primary v2 evaluation are untouched.
demand-stress-high.label: Demand stress 1.30 (scenario simulation only)
demand-stress-high.rationale: An explicitly modeled forecast-stress assumption: a 30% higher deployment-window demand tests order sizing under demand surprise without touching source facts or training.

holding-high.description: Holding multiplier 2.0; everything else identical to baseline.
holding-high.label: Holding cost doubled
holding-high.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time: a higher holding cost should push selection toward lower inventory coverage.

lead-long.description: Lead time lengthened from 3 to 5 days.
lead-long.label: Lead time 5 days
lead-long.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time on the supply assumption: a longer lead time increases the coverage base and required inventory.

lead-review-long.description: Joint stress: lead time 5 days and review period 7 days.
lead-review-long.label: Lead 5 and review 7
lead-review-long.rationale: Joint stress case: longer lead plus a weekly review compounds the coverage increase and order-timing change.

lead-short.description: Lead time shortened from 3 to 2 days.
lead-short.label: Lead time 2 days
lead-short.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time on the supply assumption: a shorter lead time reduces the coverage base and the initial inventory.

ordering-high.description: Ordering multiplier 2.0; everything else identical to baseline.
ordering-high.label: Ordering cost doubled
ordering-high.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time: a higher fixed order cost should push selection toward larger, less frequent orders.

review-weekly.description: Review period lengthened from 1 to 7 days.
review-weekly.label: Review period 7 days
review-weekly.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time on the review cadence: a weekly review changes order timing and coverage.

service-085.description: Service level target lowered from 0.90 to 0.85.
service-085.label: Service target 0.85
service-085.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time on the decision target: a lower target relaxes the constraint and may lower cost.

service-095.description: Service level target raised from 0.90 to 0.95.
service-095.label: Service target 0.95
service-095.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time on the decision target: a higher target tightens the constraint and may raise cost or force fallback.

stockout-high.description: Stockout multiplier 2.0; everything else identical to baseline.
stockout-high.label: Stockout cost doubled
stockout-high.rationale: One-factor-at-a-time: a higher stockout cost should push selection toward higher service coverage.

selection_objective: minimize total cost subject to simulated service level >= scenario target
selection_window_demand_scale: selection-window demand is never scaled: policy candidate selection always uses the observed last-validation-fold demand; a scenario demand scale applies ONLY to deployment/simulation stress and is documented per scenario
tie_break: feasible: lower total cost, then lower stockout units, then lower avg inventory, then lexicographically smaller run_id; infeasible fallback: highest simulated service level, then lower total cost, then lexicographically smaller run_id (transparent, never labeled optimal)
